title: Diagnosing the Reliability of LLM-as-a-Judge via Item Response Theory
claim: Automated judges' latent quality estimates rise with human scores but deviate systematically from the human curve, and the gap varies by task and judge.
layout: 2 stacked line plots with shared legend at right; black human line
description: Two vertically stacked line charts share a legend on the right. The top chart, titled summEval - Coherence, plots latent quality theta (y-axis, about -3 to 2) against human score 1 to 5. The bottom chart, titled VIEScore-MIE - PQ, plots theta against score 0 to 10. A thick black line with large filled circles marks the human reference. Nine thinner coloured lines with different hollow markers show judge models: GPT-4o-mini, GPT-4o, Gemini-2.5, Llama-4-Mav, Llama-4-Scout, Qwen3-235B, Qwen3-30B, Qwen3-VL-235B and Qwen3-VL-30B. In the top chart the judges cluster around the human line, and Qwen3-30B sits well below it. In the bottom chart the judges fall far below the human line, are non-monotonic at low scores, and rise sharply near 10. The fragment of a numeric table at the top of the image is unrelated to the figure.
caption: Median latent quality ($\theta$) by human score for SummEval-Coherence (up) and VIEScore-MIE PQ (down). Each line represents a different judge model; the black line denotes human.
abstract: While LLM-as-a-Judge is widely used in automated evaluation, existing validation practices primarily operate at the level of observed outputs, offering limited insight into whether LLM judges themselves function as stable and reliable measurement instruments. To address this limitation, we introduce a two-phase diagnostic framework for assessing reliability of LLM-as-a-Judge, grounded in Item Response Theory (IRT). The framework adopts Graded Response Model (GRM) of IRT and formalizes reliability along two complementary dimensions: (1) intrinsic consistency, defined as the stability of measurement behavior under prompt variations, and (2) human alignment, capturing correspondence with human quality assessments. We empirically examine diverse LLM judges with this framework, and show that leveraging IRT-GRM yields interpretable signals for diagnosing judgments systematically. These signals provide practical guidance for verifying reliablity of LLM-as-a-Judge and identifying potential causes of unreliability.
